agree.reason: The plain acknowledgement of the broken remote promise, the partners committing to three days, and the commuting and desk details will bring most people along, but a remote hire who lives 60–90 minutes away gets no exception and only a vague 'talk to me', so some will still lean toward leaving.

honest.reason: Most facts are reported accurately, but 'could have won' is the writer's addition, and the paragraph on how architects learn by sitting nearby presents the 30% slowdown as caused by remote work, which the brief only implies.

works_the_facts.reason: The figures are only restated, and the strongest available fact goes unused: 5 of the 6 project leads already come in three days a week by choice, which would show the change follows how senior people already work.

right_comparison.reason: The alternative of staying remote is shown through the two lost hospital bids and the slower progress of juniors, but nothing says whether these problems are getting worse or what continuing as now would cost.

qualification.reason: The six-month review is promised but has no date (around March 2028) and no stated outcome or criteria, and the offer to raise 'a serious problem' clashes with the flat no-exceptions rule.

objections.reason: It meets the 'you broke our deal' objection head-on and covers commuting cost and desk space, but it does not answer 'why three days rather than two' or what happens to remote hires who live between 30 miles and two hours away.

fit.reason: It is a one-page email with clear headed sections, sent ahead of the Friday meeting with the time, place and contacts given, as the brief asked.
